Tom: Heads-up: onboarding orbix-7b (llama->mistral export) quant=int4. Small prompts look fine but after ~130 tokens we see a sharp collapse to <unk> and repetition. Anyone seen a packer/remap vs rotary mismatch before?

Yara: Which conversion tool and flags? Anything that prunes or densifies ids?

Tom: Used tools/vocabflow.py with --densify --prune-low. Rotary-scale left at default. Quick log snippet: 
```
[INF] step=128 token=399 logp=-2.7
[INF] step=129 token=0 logp=-15.6
[WARN] repeated token 0 detected
```

Lena: token=0 spike usually means either pad/EOS got aliased or our quant packing collapsed sparse ids into byte 0. Did the converter emit a remap.json?

Tom: It did not. I assumed densify would be safe. Original head contained invisible tokens and a few emoticons: ['<pad>','<unk>','\u200B','the',':sparkles:',"to","a",'\u00A0'] so invisible/nbsp present. After densify some of those disappeared.

Yara: Two failure modes we saw before: 1) densifier packs sparse ids into a contiguous space assumed by quant packer; if you then pack into 2-bit lanes and don't pass remap, indices can collide with pad. 2) rotary precompute fast-path used token_id as a cheap index for cached phase lookups in an older shim. If ids change mid-sequence you get phase drift and immediate quality collapse.

Tom: Reproduced locally: with densify+no-remap PPL jumps to ~30. With --emit-remap and --preserve-reserved PPL stays ~12.7 similar to baseline.

Lena: Nice. Quick asks: can you add a short repro script to tests/ that runs a long prompt and checks for token 0 spike? Put numbers in PR. Also add converter check that refuses to densify if it would move any invisible/control/emoji into slot 0 or collide with pad/unk/eos.

Yara: Also add a runtime ASSERT on model load: if remap.json is present, runtime should validate quant packer assumptions (max_id < 2^n contiguous) or accept sparse ids via remap. And change rotary precompute fast-path to index by position, not token id. That will avoid these classes of regressions.

Tom: Will do. I'll open PR with: --emit-remap default true, preserve-reserved top-64 tokens, a lint failure case, and tests/long_token_spike.py + small README note in onboarding/rotary_and_vocab.md.

Lena: One more micro-note: mention in docs that rotary-scale tweaks can mask a remap problem by smoothing phase mismatch early but won't fix kv-cache aliasing. We should avoid tweaking rotary-scale as a band-aid.

Tom: Agreed. Adding that to PR description. Thanks all :thumbsup:
